content_voiceover: This slide reviews two pivotal trials for belantamab mafodotin, an antibody drug conjugate targeting BCMA. DREAMM-7 compared belantamab mafodotin plus bortezomib and dexamethasone, or BVd, against daratumumab plus bortezomib and dexamethasone, or DVd. The results were striking, median progression free survival was thirty six point six months with BVd versus thirteen point four months with DVd, a hazard ratio of zero point four one, highly statistically significant. DREAMM-8 compared belantamab mafodotin plus pomalidomide and dexamethasone against pomalidomide plus bortezomib and dexamethasone, again showing a clear benefit with a hazard ratio of zero point five two. Both trials, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in June twenty twenty four, support belantamab mafodotin combinations as effective options in relapsed disease. On the safety side, all grade adverse events with these combinations included thrombocytopenia in eighty seven percent, ocular adverse events in seventy nine percent, upper respiratory infection in twenty percent, anemia in nineteen percent, and pneumonia in eighteen percent. The ocular toxicity is a hallmark and defining side effect of belantamab mafodotin, presenting as keratopathy, or changes to the corneal epithelium, blurred vision, and dry eye. In these trials these events were managed with dose delays and reductions, and despite how common they were, permanent treatment discontinuation due solely to ocular toxicity was relatively uncommon.
keypoints: DREAMM-7 showed BVd had median PFS of 36.6 months versus 13.4 months for DVd
DREAMM-8 showed belantamab-pomalidomide-dexamethasone outperformed PVd, HR 0.52
Ocular toxicity, especially keratopathy, is the hallmark side effect of belantamab mafodotin
Ocular events are managed with dose delays and reductions rather than discontinuation
keypoint_voiceover: Remember belantamab mafodotin combinations dramatically improved progression free survival in both DREAMM-7 and DREAMM-8, but the tradeoff is a very high rate of ocular toxicity, especially keratopathy, which is managed with dose modification rather than stopping the drug outright in most patients.
